title: The Last Current
premise: Yara Halloran, a salvage diver who never stays anywhere longer than a season, is hired by her old rival Cassian Voss to recover a sealed vault from the Meridian, a naval research vessel that sank under circumstances the navy has spent twenty years burying. As the crew descends, Yara discovers the wreck holds not treasure but evidence of an experiment that erased the memories of everyone aboard—including her own mother, whose disappearance Yara has been running from ever since. The navy's fixers close in on the expedition, and Voss reveals he intends to sell the data to the highest bidder rather than expose it. In the end, Yara must choose between destroying the truth that could restore her identity and using it against the people who took everything—choosing neither, she floods the vault forever, keeps only one fragment of her mother's voice, and finally allows herself to stop moving.
about_author: Beatrix Almeida is a former maritime archaeologist who spent six years cataloguing wrecks off the Atlantic shelf before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a houseboat in Nova Scotia, where the tide dictates her working hours.

chapters.title: Salt in the Wires
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Working a routine salvage off a decommissioned buoy field, Yara finds a navy transponder fused into wreckage that shouldn't exist there. Her crewmate Dez warns her to drop it; she can't. Emotional beat: restlessness as armor—the chapter establishes why Yara never stays anywhere long enough to be found.

chapters.title: The Man Who Kept Score
chapters.summary: Cassian Voss arrives at the harbor bar with a contract: salvage rights to the Meridian, coordinates included, payment triple the crew's yearly take. Yara refuses; her first mate Odile quietly signs anyway, revealing the crew is broke. Emotional beat: old rivalry curdling into obligation.

chapters.title: Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter from Yara's POV: twenty years ago, her mother served aboard the Meridian and vanished when it sank. Yara's father made the crew swear off the site before he died. Now she breaks the oath herself. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. The crew preps the dive vessel Thessaly while a navy patrol boat idles suspiciously offshore. Odile reveals she's mortgaged her own boat to fund the job. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by desperation; the crew becomes family on paper again.

chapters.title: Down to the Cold
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. First descent to the Meridian at 90 meters. The wreck is wrong—hull breached from the inside, corridors scorched but cargo intact. She finds a sealed vault door stamped with her mother's unit designation. Emotional beat: awe shading into dread.

chapters.title: What the Navy Won't Discuss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He briefs the crew on the mission's true target: a black-box archive, not valuables. He lies about why. A navy helicopter overflies the Thessaly twice. Emotional beat: the reader learns Voss knows more than he says, and enjoys knowing it.

chapters.title: The Inside Job
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Second dive through the interior. She recovers a crew logbook and finds her mother's handwriting describing 'the quieting'—an experiment that worked too well. Decompression sickness nearly kills her dive partner Renn. Emotional beat: personal history surfacing like a body.

chapters.title: Logbook of the Quieting
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Deciphering the logbook overnight: the Meridian hosted a memory-erasure trial on its own crew. The last entry names survivors transferred ashore—one matching Yara's mother's service number. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as horror.

chapters.title: Visitors
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Two men claiming to be coast guard board the Thessaly, asking precise questions about their survey grid. Voss handles them smoothly; afterward he admits they were navy fixers. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening; nowhere left to run on open water.

chapters.title: Pressure Limits
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Recovering from his bends hit, Renn argues the dives are beyond safe margins. Yara pushes for one more. The crew splits—Odile sides with Yara, Dez with Renn. Emotional beat: the cost of obsession made physical.

chapters.title: Mother Tongue
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Third dive: she cracks the vault's outer seal and retrieves a single data core plus a personal effects locker containing her mother's voice recorder. On ascent, sonar shows the navy ship changing course toward them. Emotional beat: triumph immediately shadowed by pursuit.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, alone at night. The recorder plays: her mother describing the experiment's purpose—not erasing memory, but rewriting identity—and volunteering to prove it reversible. Her final entry cuts mid-sentence. Emotional beat: devastating intimacy; Yara hears her mother's voice for the first time in twenty years.

chapters.title: Voss's Ledger
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He reveals to Yara that he was aboard the support ship twenty years ago; his brother was Meridian crew. He doesn't want exposure—he wants to sell the technology back to a private buyer. Emotional beat: rival revealed as mirror image, both children of the same wound.

chapters.title: Mutiny Weather
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A storm front traps the Thessaly in the survey zone. The navy ship closes in. Dez discovers Voss has been transmitting position data to the buyer. Crew vote: finish the job or scuttle it. Emotional beat: trust fracturing under pressure like a hull.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Shadow
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. The buyer's private security vessel appears—a converted trawler with armed crew. Voss negotiates handoff of the core at dawn. Yara realizes once it leaves the Thessaly, her mother's story dies in a vault. Emotional beat: cornered clarity.

chapters.title: Last Dive
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Against the storm and both navies, Yara makes an unsanctioned final descent to plant charges on the vault itself—if she can't keep the truth, no one will. Renn insists on diving backup despite his injury. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely, fear mastered.

chapters.title: Ninety Meters Down
chapters.summary: Dual-tension climax part one. Yara reaches the vault as the navy deploys divers of its own. Underwater confrontation in zero visibility; Renn takes a bullet graze shielding the charge line. Emotional beat: pure survival adrenaline, the book's most kinetic sequence.

chapters.title: What It Found
chapters.summary: Climax part two, Yara's POV. Surface chaos: Voss tries to deliver the core, Dez disables the transfer, the buyer's men board, and the navy ship trains searchlights on everyone. Yara detonates the vault remotely, then plays her mother's recording over the Thessaly's loudspeakers for all parties to hear. Emotional beat: truth as detonation—she gives away the secret to destroy its value.

chapters.title: Aftermath Water
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Standoff dissolves: the buyer withdraws, the navy detains Voss, and the recording forces an internal scandal that will take years to play out. The Thessaly limps home with a damaged hull and a crew that survived what should have ended them. Emotional beat: exhausted relief, debts acknowledged.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Weeks later, giving testimony to a naval inquiry, Yara chooses to tell the whole truth about the Meridian, accepting she may never dive commercially again. She learns her mother survived the sinking and lived three more years under a new name. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed through honesty rather than records.

chapters.title: Anchorage
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. The crew repairs the Thessaly together; Odile's mortgage is paid by an anonymous settlement Yara quietly arranged from the inquiry's whistleblower provision. Renn returns to diving. Emotional beat: home rebuilt not as a place but as people who stayed.

chapters.title: The Current That Stays
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, closing chapter. At her mother's unmarked grave, Yara buries the voice recorder after copying one fragment—her mother saying her childhood nickname—to keep. For the first time, she signs a lease. Final image: the harbor at dusk, the Thessaly at anchor, Yara watching the tide come in without checking the time. Emotional beat: stillness earned; the running stops.
